comparisons.peer_summary: Restructuring and other charges recognized in operating expenses were $1,533 million in fiscal year 2024 and $244 million in fiscal year 2023. The 2024 charges primarily consisted of employee termination costs related to cost reduction activities associated with the VMware Merger, while the 2023 charges were primarily non-recurring charges related to IP litigation.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose significant restructuring and cost-reduction charges within their operating expenses for the fiscal year. Intel explicitly attributes a $3.1 billion decrease in Intel Products operating expenses to 'cost-reduction measures across all of our Intel Products operating segments.' Similarly, Broadcom reports $1,533 million in restructuring and other charges in 2024 operating expenses, primarily driven by 'employee termination costs from cost reduction activities related to the VMware Merger.' While both cite cost reduction as a driver, Intel reports a net decrease in segment operating expenses due to these measures, whereas Broadcom reports a large net increase in restructuring charges compared to the prior year, reflecting different scales and timing of integration-related costs.

sentences.text: Total Intel Products operating expenses were $12.2 billion in 2023, down $3.1 billion from 2022, primarily driven by various cost-reduction measures across all of our Intel Products operating segments.
Restructuring and other charges recognized in operating expenses were $1,533 million and $244 million in fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The fiscal year 2024 charges primarily included employee termination costs from cost reduction activities related to the VMware Merger.

comparisons.peer_topic: Operating Expense Drivers and Prior Year Comparison
comparisons.peer_summary: Operating expenses increased for fiscal year 2024 due to growth in employees and compensation increases, while the prior year included a $1.4 billion acquisition termination charge related to the proposed Arm transaction.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA discuss the primary drivers of their operating expense changes year-over-year. Intel highlights that its Intel Products operating expenses decreased by $3.1 billion, primarily driven by 'various cost-reduction measures.' In contrast, NVIDIA reports that its operating expenses increased in fiscal year 2024, 'driven by growth in employees and compensation increases.' This highlights a divergence in expense management: Intel successfully reduced expenses through cost-cutting, while NVIDIA's expenses grew due to headcount and compensation growth, likely supporting its expansion.
